title: probe-based fastpath gating with lightweight consistency checks and safe-mode fallback
author: Asha Varma
description:
Motivation: transient kernel incompatibilities and scheduling pressure occasionally cause our fast (kernel-optimized) codepath to emit subtly different attention corner-cases compared to the stable slow path. This manifests as rare correctness drift under tight latency budgets when we aggressively favor the fast path. This PR introduces a low-overhead probe-and-validate gating mechanism plus a conservative "safe-mode" fallback to ensure correctness while preserving most of the fast-path win.

What this changes (summary):
- Fast-path probe: before switching a worker to a new fast kernel variant, the worker runs a tiny micro-benchmark (probe) that exercises attention edge-cases (short prefix, long memory, kv cache reuse) and computes a compact validation token (rolling hash + checksum) of the probe outputs.
- Lightweight consistency checks: the probe token is compared against an expected token for that kernel/model/seqconfig. Mismatches block the fast-path and create a diagnostic event.
- Safe-mode fallback: on mismatch or repeated probe failures the worker enters safe-mode: it routes requests to the stable slow kernel and uses a conservative precision profile (FP32/FP16 fallback sequence) to maximize parity. Safe-mode is scoped per-host and decays after a successful probe window.
- KV-cache-aware probing: probes are run both with empty and primed KV cache to catch cache-dependent divergences; we avoid draining real live KV entries by using a local ephemeral cache snapshot.
- Scheduling integration: scheduler adds a probe budget per epoch and prefers low-latency probes during low-util periods; probes are throttled to avoid affecting p99.
- Observability and rollback: new metrics (probe_success, probe_failure_reason, safe_mode_entries, safe_mode_duration) and a diagnostic payload attached to failure events; a quick flip flag inserted in config to disable probes or force safe-mode for emergency mitigation.

Checklist:
- [x] unit tests for probe harness and checksum comparison
- [x] integration tests exercising primed/unprimed KV paths
- [x] end-to-end canary on benchmark-lab with 3 models (gpt-small, gpt-medium, opt-6b)
- [x] dashboards for probe metrics and alerts on elevated failure rates
- [x] rollout plan and rollback flag in runtime config

Performance impact: canary results show median latency change +1% on typical sequences; tail impact negligible when probe budget is set to 1 probe per 10k requests per host. When fast-path is allowed, token throughput improved by 7-11% on our CPU+GPU mixed pools for served sequence-length distribution used in ENG-5421. Safe-mode incurs expected cost (2–3x token CPU work) but is scoped to affected hosts and decays quickly once a stable kernel/probe pair is validated.

Testing notes:
- benchmark-lab run id: bl-2025-11-26-ffprobe (attached metrics snapshot in PR artifacts)
- Integration harness includes a synthetic adversarial suite that ramps KV re-use patterns to surface cache-dependent bugs.

Compatibility and migration:
- Probe tokens are versioned by (model_hash, kernel_variant, seq_profile, probe_version). When loading older kernels that lack tokens the system treats them as probe-missing and will perform a full validation run the first time (safe-mode until validated).
- No model API changes. All config is behind runtime feature flag fastpath_probe_enabled (default ON in canary, default OFF in prod until we complete broader rollout).

Rollout plan:
1. Merge to main -> internal canary (benchmark-lab) for 48 hours.
2. Gradual rollout to Hosted low-traffic region (10% hosts) and monitor probe_failure_rate < 0.1%.
3. Expand to Dedicated pools, then set fastpath_probe_enabled ON for most fleets.
4. If probe failure spikes, flip fastpath_probe_enabled to OFF or force safe-mode (operator fix).

Notes on correctness tradeoffs: the design intentionally keeps probes compact to avoid p99 regressions; this means very rare divergence types might not be caught immediately and will surface as diagnostic events or user reports. The safe-mode provides a deterministic recovery path for these cases.

Related: references ENG-5421 (kernel stability), ENG-5490 (kv cache priming heuristics).

review_conversation: Miguel Ortega: Left a detailed comment about the potential for probe overhead to affect p99; suggested adding scheduler safeguards. Asha: added probe_budget and throttling in scheduler and re-ran canary.
Lena Park: Requested stronger telemetry around 'why' a probe failed (checksum vs. crash). Asha: split failure reasons and added probe_failure_reason label (checksum|crash|timeout|vc_mismatch).
Jordan Chen: Asked for safe-mode decay semantics. Asha: implemented exponential decay (success window of 5 consecutive probes to exit).
QA (automated): initial CI run showed one flaky integration test (kv-adversary) failing intermittently — test updated to be less timing-sensitive and re-run.
release_notes: Introduce probe-based fastpath gating with lightweight validation tokens and a per-host safe-mode fallback. Adds probe metrics and a runtime flag to disable probes in emergencies. Improves fast-path safety with minimal median-latency impact; can be rolled back via config.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the probe payload minimal; future work (ENG-5602) will expand probe coverage if we can maintain the same budget constraints.
